## Body

#135 (plan 206, s15) merged at bb753b8. Lessons from its final rounds (2266c8a, 565c818, 46463da), beyond the round-3 note:

- PM messages cross pushes in bursts. Five near-identical pm-001 sends arrived after the head they asked for was already pushed. Before acting on one, compare it with the current head and the PR body. If it's already done, answer once with the head and the commit that holds each item. Don't push again and don't re-answer every echo.
- Contract decisions pm-001 accepted (reuse them, don't relitigate):
  - --drop-queued withdraws all or nothing: any failed FYI hold refuses with E-RS-DIRECTORY-NOT-TOLD and the landed retire is never rolled back; the same command retries.
  - A requester that is no longer a seat (NoRegistryEntry / SeatIsGone from hold_fyi) is told "gone", still withdrawn, listed in data.gone, and its event says requester_gone.
  - Prefer making a bad state unreachable, and name the invariant (comments at each path, plus the PR body), over adding a recovery path you can only test by seeding. Example: a requeue can't land behind a retired role.
- When you ship a verb another merged PR parked as "not shipped" (#141's Recommendation.later), grep its tests for the pin (later, E-RS-UNPORTED, "not shipped"). There were three.
- Retained-ID trap: a retired role's role.dd.json stays, so any "add <id>" recommendation for it is unusable. Recommendations built from active-only lists must treat retired IDs separately: picture::retarget emits one ddocs set --value-json per unfinished step.
- Break a store table to force a hold failure in a test: ALTER TABLE fyis RENAME TO fyis_away over a raw sqlx connection to rig._fresh.path(), then rename it back.
- Plan 215 starts on a local branch coder/215-holdings-followups in ~/pi-hacking/fleet-215-holdings-followups, because pm-001's worktree has plan/215 checked out. Push with HEAD:plan/215-holdings-followups.
